beats.text: You're in a room with twenty-three people. Two of them probably share a birthday.
Three hundred sixty-five days. Twenty-three birthdays. Sounds unlikely.
Half of them have a match! With seventy people, almost every room.
Twenty-three people make two hundred fifty-three pairs. That's why

sources: Birthday problem (probability theory; e.g. von Mises 1939): with 23 people the chance that at least two share a birthday is 50.7 %; with 70 people 99.9 % (365 equally likely days, no leap years). 23 people form 253 pairs.
